city_fields.supportSceneAlt: Calming birth center suite at Canyon Midwifery, Peoria's CABC-accredited freestanding birth center
city_fields.culture: Peoria is a northwest-valley city of roughly 200,000 people strung along Loop 101 between Glendale and the West Wing mountains, and it has grown from an old farming town into one of metro Phoenix's biggest family suburbs. Vistancia and Terrace Park fill up with young households, so the city supports a full local set of birth services: it has its own freestanding birth center, a hospital maternity program minutes away in Sun City West, and independent Peoria doulas serving families across the city alongside the valley's larger practices. Most Peoria births happen at Banner Del E. Webb Medical Center or Abrazo Arrowhead Campus across the Loop 101, and both hospitals draw a steady share of their maternity volume from Peoria addresses.
city_fields.medicaidNote: Yes \u2014 Arizona Medicaid (AHCCCS) covers doula services as of October 1, 2024 for all pregnant and postpartum members, but only through doulas certified by ADHS and registered with AHCCCS. Ask any doula you interview whether they are state-certified and AHCCCS-enrolled; private-pay doulas can still set up payment plans. Call 602-417-4000 (AHCCCS) or check your health plan's provider list to find enrolled doulas.
